question: What caused the Amazon Web Services outage in October 2025, and what did it disrupt?
text:
The **October 20, 2025 AWS outage** was caused by a bug in the automated system that manages DNS for **Amazon DynamoDB** in AWS’s Northern Virginia region (`us-east-1`). Two automated updates ran in an unexpected order—a *race condition*—leaving the database service’s regional address with an empty DNS record. Services that depended on that address could no longer connect to DynamoDB. ([aws.amazon.com](https://aws.amazon.com/message/101925/))

The failure then cascaded: AWS had trouble launching new **EC2 virtual servers**, and some **Network Load Balancers** had connection failures. Those problems continued for hours after the original DNS issue was fixed. ([aws.amazon.com](https://aws.amazon.com/message/101925/))

Although the fault began in one AWS region, users worldwide saw disruptions. Affected services included **Snapchat, Reddit, Signal, Slack, Roblox, Fortnite, and Venmo**, as well as Amazon’s own **Ring and Alexa**. ([pbs.org](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/nation/amazon-cloud-computing-outage-disrupts-snapchat-ring-and-many-other-online-services?utm_source=openai))
